message.text: I'm going to write a script that extracts all top-level function names from the internal/ directory's non-test Go files, then counts how many times each function gets called across the entire repository, accounting for both direct function calls and method invocations while excluding generated proto code and web directories.

args.command:
cd /bench/repo && cat > /tmp/fanin.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Collect declarations under internal/ (non-test)
decls=$(grep -rhn --include=*.go -E '^func ' internal/ --exclude='*_test.go' \
  | sed -E 's/^[0-9]+:func (\([^)]*\) )?([A-Za-z0-9_]+)\(.*/\2/' | sort -u)

for name in $decls; do
  # count call sites across repo non-test go files, excluding generated proto and the declaration lines
  n=$(grep -rhoE "(\.|[^A-Za-z0-9_.])${name}\(" --include=*.go . \
      --exclude='*_test.go' --exclude='*.pb.go' --exclude='*.pb.gw.go' --exclude='*.connect.go' \
      | wc -l)
  d=$(grep -rhcE "^func (\([^)]*\) )?${name}\(" --include=*.go . --exclude='*_test.go' 2>/dev/null | paste -sd+ | bc)
  echo "$n $name"
done | sort -nr | head -40
EOF
bash /tmp/fanin.sh

I see the issue with simple name matching—it picks up unrelated identifiers across different contexts. I need to count qualified function calls instead, tracking the package context for each symbol and matching calls like `pkg.Name(` for exported functions or `.Name(` for methods, being careful to attribute them correctly. For each symbol, I'll determine which package it's declared in and then count only the calls that match that specific context.

Some candidates stand out as having higher usage: functions in the `filter` package that get called across different store drivers, utilities in `util.*`, `base.GenUUID` appearing 7 times, and `profile.AllowAnonymous`. Let me compute these qualified counts properly to get accurate numbers.
The naive name counting conflates identifiers across packages, so let me count package-qualified call sites.

args.command:
cd /bench/repo && while IFS=$'\t' read -r name loc; do
  file="${loc%%:*}"
  pkg=$(head -3 "$file" | grep -m1 '^package ' | awk '{print $2}')
  dir=$(dirname "$file")
  # qualified external calls: pkg.Name(
  ext=$(grep -rhoE "\b${pkg}\.${name}\(" --include=*.go $(cat /tmp/gofiles.txt) 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
  # intra-package unqualified calls (exclude declaration lines)
  intra=$(grep -hoE "(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_.])${name}\(" $(ls $dir/*.go 2>/dev/null | grep -v '_test.go') 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
  decls=$(grep -hcE "^func (\([^)]*\) )?${name}\(" $(ls $dir/*.go 2>/dev/null | grep -v '_test.go') 2>/dev/null | awk '{s+=$1} END{print s+0}')
  intra=$(( intra - decls ))
  echo -e "$((ext+intra))\t$ext\t$intra\t$name\t$loc"
done < /tmp/decls.tsv | sort -nr | head -25

cd /bench/repo && while IFS=$'\t' read -r name loc recv; do
  file="${loc%%:*}"; dir=$(dirname "$file")
  pkg=$(grep -m1 '^package ' "$file" | awk '{print $2}')
  [ -z "$pkg" ] && pkg="UNKNOWNPKG"
  pkgfiles=$(ls $dir/*.go 2>/dev/null | grep -v '_test.go')
  decls=$(grep -hE "^func (\([^)]*\) )?${name}\(" $pkgfiles 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
  intra=$(( $(grep -hoE "(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_.])${name}\(" $pkgfiles 2>/dev/null | wc -l) - decls ))
  if [ -n "$recv" ]; then
    kind=method
    ext=$(grep -hoE "\.${name}\(" $(cat /tmp/gofiles.txt) 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
    ext=$(( ext - $(grep -hoE "\.${name}\(" $pkgfiles 2>/dev/null | wc -l) ))
  else
    kind=func
    ext=$(grep -hoE "(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])${pkg}\.${name}\(" $(cat /tmp/gofiles.txt) 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
  fi
  echo -e "$((ext+intra))\t$ext\t$intra\t$kind\t$name\t$loc\t$recv"
done < /tmp/decls2.tsv | sort -nr > /tmp/fanin_result.tsv; head -30 /tmp/fanin_result.tsv

`addArg` is the one-stop helper for binding a value into the generated SQL: it appends to `r.args`, bumps `r.placeholderCounter`, and returns the dialect-correct placeholder (`$N` for Postgres, `?` otherwise). Because every literal in a compiled filter expression has to go through it, nearly every render branch calls it — `grep -c 'r\.addArg('` on that file gives 28 matching lines with 28 occurrences.

How I measured, and the runners-up: I extracted all 272 non-test `func` declarations under `internal/`, then counted call sites across all non-test, non-generated Go files (195 files, excluding `*_test.go`, `*.pb.go`, `*.pb.gw.go`, `*.connect.go`, and `web/`). Package-level functions were counted as `pkg.Name(` plus unqualified same-package calls; methods as `.Name(`, then hand-verified by receiver.
